title: National Financial Inclusion Strategies
summary: How to develop, govern and implement a national financial inclusion strategy, setting priorities and targets and aligning ministries, regulators and the private sector.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to develop, govern and implement a national financial inclusion strategy, setting priorities and targets and aligning ministries, regulators and the private sector.
Learning Objectives: Design the structure, priorities and targets of a national strategy
Establish governance and coordination for implementation
Monitor progress with a results framework
Syllabus: Diagnostics, stakeholder engagement and priority setting
Governance: steering committees, working groups and secretariats
Public sector levers: government payments, postal networks and state banks
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries, treasuries and central banks responsible for financial inclusion and consumer policy
Staff of consumer protection agencies, ombudsman schemes and financial education bodies
Legislative drafters, legal advisers and parliamentary committee staff working on consumer and financial inclusion legislation
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services, social or consumer policy is helpful. No technical background in financial regulation is required.
Core Reading: G20/OECD (2022), High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection
World Bank (2017), Good Practices for Financial Consumer Protection
OECD (2020), Recommendation of the Council on Financial Literacy
CPMI and World Bank (2016), Payment Aspects of Financial Inclusion
World Bank (2022), The Global Findex Database 2021: Financial Inclusion, Digital Payments, and Resilience in the Age of COVID-19
